definitions.explanation: replacing someone in an official position, often a high-ranking person, typically due to poor performance or scandal

examples.japanese: {大臣|だいじん}が{更迭|こうてつ}された。
{監督|かんとく}の{更迭|こうてつ}が{発表|はっぴょう}された。
examples.english: The replacement of the manager was announced.

examples.japanese: {不祥事|ふしょうじ}の{責任|せきにん}を{取|と}り、{社長|しゃちょう}が{更迭|こうてつ}された。
examples.english: The president was removed from his position, taking responsibility for the scandal.

notes:
{更迭|こうてつ} means to replace or remove someone from an official position, often used in political and business contexts.

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
- {更|こう} (change, renew)
- {迭|てつ} (alternate, replace)

USAGE:
- {更迭|こうてつ}する (to replace/remove - suru verb)
- {更迭|こうてつ}される (to be replaced/removed)
- 〜を{更迭|こうてつ}する (to remove ~ from position)

COMMON CONTEXTS:
- {大臣|だいじん}の{更迭|こうてつ} (cabinet reshuffle)
- {監督|かんとく}の{更迭|こうてつ} (manager replacement in sports)
- {幹部|かんぶ}の{更迭|こうてつ} (executive reshuffle)

NUANCE:
- Often implies removal due to failure, scandal, or pressure
- More formal than {交代|こうたい} (replacement/rotation)
- Common in news reporting

RELATED TERMS:
- {解任|かいにん} (dismissal)
- {辞任|じにん} (resignation)
- {交代|こうたい} (replacement - neutral term)
